title: Calculation reproducibility
question: Does the chart reproduce independent astronomical and Human Design references?
method: Use fixed UTC instants, explicit coordinates, timezone versions, node conventions and reference outputs. Include boundary cases and birth-time uncertainty.
expected: Matching positions and derived gates within a tolerance fixed before the run.
notExpected: Personality validity, purpose, or psychological effects.
falsification: Any repeated mismatch beyond the declared tolerance rejects the implementation for that domain.
baseline: Independent ephemeris, saved reference fixtures, and the supplied free-human-design engine.

title: Blinded chart matching
question: Can people identify their chart-derived description above chance?
method: Randomize one actual and three decoy descriptions, equalize length and tone, conceal birth data and chart labels from raters. Lock one choice per participant.
expected: Accuracy above 25%, with a preregistered meaningful margin and confidence interval.
notExpected: A pleasing description or a single correct guess is not evidence.
falsification: A powered equivalence test contained within the preregistered near-chance interval contradicts meaningful matching ability; wide intervals are inconclusive.
baseline: Four-choice chance and generic equally positive descriptions.

title: Prospective prediction
question: Do frozen chart predictions improve forecasts of later measured behavior?
method: Register outcome, time window, probability, chart version, model fingerprint and scoring rule before outcomes. Never edit the prediction; append corrections.
expected: Lower held-out Brier score than the locked baseline by a preregistered useful margin.
notExpected: Retrospective stories, edited predictions, or forecast confidence alone.
falsification: A precise null improvement or worse held-out score contradicts the stated predictive advantage.
baseline: Personal historical base rate, questionnaire-only model, shuffled charts, and chart-free local model.

title: Randomized cultivation trial
question: Does chart-personalized practice help more than equally attentive generic practice?
method: Randomly assign consenting adults to personalized or matched generic exercises. Fix the primary wellbeing measure and duration, record adherence, analyze all assigned participants, and document attrition.
expected: A meaningful between-group change with uncertainty reported.
notExpected: Improvement alone does not validate astrology; attention and expectation can help both groups.
falsification: A sufficiently precise effect below the preregistered minimum useful difference contradicts the added benefit claim.
baseline: Same model, contact time, exercise difficulty, and supportive language without chart personalization.

title: Resonance network prediction
question: Do declared relational features predict later mutual connection?
method: Use opt-in pseudonymous pairs, record connection outcomes independently from both people, freeze features, hold out entire people and pairs, and allow withdrawal.
expected: Better held-out prediction than shared interests, prior familiarity and baseline sociability.
notExpected: Chart similarity is not a measured bond or permission to contact someone.
falsification: No useful incremental held-out accuracy with adequate precision contradicts the network prediction claim.
baseline: Interest-only matching and permuted chart-to-person assignments.

title: Perspective and ablation test
question: Do the five perspective views add measurable information?
method: Keep event coordinates and original observations immutable. Append reinterpretations with timestamps. Compare the full system with one perspective or chart input withheld, using the same model and unseen tasks.
expected: Improved locked task scores and provenance retention across held-out contexts.
notExpected: Duplicating one placement across five named views does not create five independent observations.
falsification: No incremental predictive benefit rejects the added-information claim; any overwritten historical observation fails the preservation rule.
